title: Dimension of a constructible subset and its closure over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $S\subseteq |T|$ be constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset], and let $\overline S$ be its Zariski closure. Give both subsets the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology] and measure their topological Krull dimensions by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the empty set of dimension $-\infty$. Then
$$ \dim S=\dim\overline S.$$
No assertion of this kind is made for an arbitrary subset of $T$, or for an arbitrary Noetherian scheme not of finite type over a field.

source.place: Tag 00OT, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, proof of (1)=(2), where every nonempty open in an irreducible component retains its dimension; consequence for a finite locally closed decomposition of a constructible subset

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, its closure is empty and both dimensions are $-\infty$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume $S\ne\varnothing$. By [def-weil-constructible-subset], write $S=\bigcup_{a=1}^r L_a$ with each $L_a=U_a\cap F_a$ locally closed, $U_a$ open and $F_a$ closed in $|T|$; discard empty pieces. Put $Z_a=\overline{L_a}$ in $|T|$. Since $Z_a\subseteq F_a$ and $L_a\subseteq U_a$, we have $L_a=U_a\cap Z_a$. Also $Z=\overline S=\bigcup_a Z_a$: the finite union on the right is closed and contains $S$, and each $Z_a$ is contained in $\overline S$.

source.place: Tags 0055 (definition-Krull) and 005G/005L: finite locally closed decomposition and finite-union closure calculation

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, generated by $0$ and $1$. Its spectrum is a one-point affine scheme, hence quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $T$ Noetherian. For every $a$, apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] to the closed subset $Z_a$ of $T$. It gives a finite cover $Z_a=\bigcup_{b=1}^{m_a} C_{ab}$ by its distinct irreducible components, which are closed in $Z_a$, hence in $|T|$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); finite closed-component decomposition from Properties Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components) and Topology Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian)

proof.text: Fix $a,b$. The component $C_{ab}$ is not contained in the union of the other $C_{ac}$: otherwise irreducibility would force containment in one of them, contradicting maximality and distinctness in [def-weil-irreducible-components]. (The finite-union assertion follows by induction from the defining two-closed-set condition.) Therefore $O_{ab}=Z_a\setminus\bigcup_{c\ne b}C_{ac}$ is a nonempty open subset of $Z_a$ contained in $C_{ab}$. Density of $L_a$ in $Z_a$ implies $O_{ab}\cap L_a\ne\varnothing$. Hence $V_{ab}=U_a\cap C_{ab}=L_a\cap C_{ab}$ is a nonempty open subset of $C_{ab}$ contained in $S$. All these topologies are the subspace topologies of [def-kun-subspace-topology].

source.place: Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian), proof of (3): remove the other components; density supplies the intersection

proof.text: Give $C_{ab}$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its underlying space is exactly $C_{ab}$ with the subspace topology: the closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its image by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It is an irreducible scheme because $C_{ab}$ is irreducible. It is locally of finite type over $k$: on a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $T$ with $A$ finitely generated over $k$ as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], its inverse images are $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by the cited reduced-structure lemma. Images of any finite set of algebra generators of $A$ generate $A/I$, so these charts give the required locally finite type structure. No separatedness or algebraic closure of $k$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), affine construction; locally finite type condition checked directly on its quotient charts

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] to the irreducible $k$-scheme with underlying space $C_{ab}$ from Step 4 and to its nonempty open $V_{ab}$ from Step 3. The locally finite type hypothesis was checked in Step 4, and the cited statement explicitly permits irreducible schemes without a reducedness assumption. We obtain $\dim C_{ab}=\dim V_{ab}$. These are the topological dimensions of the subsets in the statement, since the underlying space of the reduced induced scheme is the same subspace.

source.place: Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), part (3); scheme version of the open-dimension calculation of Algebra Tag 00OT

proof.text: For any inclusion of subspaces $A\subseteq B$, closing each term $D_j$ of a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $A$ in $B$ preserves its length. Indeed $A\cap\overline{D_j}^{\,B}=D_j$, so the inclusions remain strict; and the closure is irreducible, since a cover of it by two closed sets restricts to such a cover of the dense irreducible $D_j$, forcing $D_j$, and then its closure, into one of the two sets. Thus the chain definition in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] gives $\dim A\le\dim B$ (including empty subspaces). Apply this to $S\subseteq Z$ to get $\dim S\le\dim Z$, and to $V_{ab}\subseteq S$ to get $\dim C_{ab}=\dim V_{ab}\le\dim S$.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull): closure-of-chains proof of subspace dimension monotonicity

proof.text: The finite family $C_{ab}$ covers $Z$ and each member is closed in $Z$. If $D_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq D_n$ is a chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $Z$, its largest member $D_n$ is covered by the finitely many closed subsets $D_n\cap C_{ab}$. By induction on this finite family, the defining irreducibility condition of [def-weil-irreducible-components] puts $D_n$ inside one $C_{ab}$. Then every $D_j$ is closed and irreducible in that $C_{ab}$, with its inclusions still strict. Hence $n\le\dim C_{ab}\le\dim S$ by Steps 5–6. Taking the supremum of all such lengths, as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], proves $\dim Z\le\dim S$. Together with Step 6, this proves the claimed equality.
